one_liner: Python imaging-codec package over libdeflate, libspng, libjpeg-turbo, OpenJPEG and libjxl, with its own TIFF LZW decoder about 2x faster than imagecodecs'.
what_it_does: opencodecs is a Python package (Cython plus C/C++ extensions, about 40 compiled modules per wheel) that covers the ground of imagecodecs and part of tifffile. It offers byte compressors, image codecs (PNG, JPEG, JPEG 2000, HTJ2K, JPEG XL, AVIF, HEIF, WebP, JPEG-LS, BCn), scientific array codecs, and native readers for TIFF, OME-TIFF, CZI, NDTiff, OME-Zarr, DICOM and other containers, with HTTP range requests and per-tile thread pools. The API is its own: oc.read/oc.write, oc.get_codec(name).encode/decode and Reader objects, not imagecodecs' png_encode-style functions, although many keyword names (filter=, strategy=, level=) follow imagecodecs. For C or C++ users the only directly reusable new code is the MIT-licensed TIFF LZW codec in 3rdparty/oc_tifflzw/; everything else wraps existing C libraries.
how_it_is_fast: The TIFF LZW decoder (oc_tifflzw.c) gives each dictionary entry a pointer and a length into output it has already written, so a code decodes as one copy. Strings of up to 16 bytes move as one or two 8-byte chunks, and literals point into a padded constant table. imagecodecs instead walks each code's linked prefix chain backwards. This is the 'output buffer as dictionary' idea also used by the AnimatedGIF Turbo mode. The other gains come from backend and threading choices rather than new algorithms: PNG and deflate use libdeflate's whole-buffer compressor instead of zlib; JPEG uses a SIMD build of libjpeg-turbo; JPEG 2000, JPEG XL and BC1-BC7 decode run on several threads by default (BCn in row bands through a vendored bcdec with a BC7 fast path for modes without secondary indices). The TIFF reader decompresses a batch of tiles, undoes the predictor and places them in one native call that releases the GIL once.
when_to_use: Python pipelines that read LZW-compressed TIFF strips or tiles: the LZW decoder is about 2.2x faster than imagecodecs.lzw_decode like for like (enricher rerun, below) and 2.9-3.3x in the README's harness.

Python scientific-imaging readers (TIFF, OME-TIFF, CZI, NDTiff, OME-Zarr, DICOM WSI) over NVMe, NAS or S3, where per-tile parallel decode and HTTP range reads matter more than single-codec speed. The README measures 1.3x-13.2x over tifffile, depending on threads and readers, but no harness for that table is in bench/.

Getting libdeflate-backed PNG and zlib-stream encoding (about 2.6x faster than zlib level 6 on the README's data) without assembling the C libraries yourself, if you accept about 0.9% larger PNG output.
Multi-threaded JPEG 2000 or JPEG XL encode and decode from a single Python call on an otherwise idle machine, where imagecodecs' default runs one thread.
C or C++ projects that need a small, permissively licensed TIFF LZW encoder and decoder: vendor 3rdparty/oc_tifflzw/ (MIT, plain C).
when_not_to_use: As evidence that its codecs are faster per core: the JPEG 2000, JPEG XL, BC1 and BC7 rows compare several threads against one. Per CPU-second, derived from the result files, opencodecs is about 0.63x on Linux JPEG 2000 encode (703.76 / (151.07 x 7.4)), 0.82x on Mac BC1 decode and 1.05x on Mac BC7 decode.

Expecting the README's JPEG gains on any machine. The Linux 3.91x encode and 1.80x decode rows measure an imagecodecs wheel whose libjpeg-turbo has no SIMD (see verified_claims_summary). On Windows, where that is not the case, the rows are 0.97x and 1.01x.

When you already use imagecodecs' libdeflate codec (deflate_encode). In the enricher rerun it wrote byte-identical 30,524,176-byte output at level 6 in 519 ms against opencodecs' 537 ms, so the README's 2.6x deflate encode win disappears.

Byte compressors (zstd, lz4, brotli, blosc2, lzma, bz2, snappy), WebP, QOI, JPEG-LS, LERC decode and ZFP: they wrap the same libraries as imagecodecs and land at 0.70x-1.26x. ZFP encode is 0.72x on the Mac and 0.70x on Windows.

Risk-averse or C++-only projects: one author, 3 stars, six PyPI releases in seven days (0.3.1 on 2026-09-28 to 0.7.1 on 2026-10-04), and changelogs that keep fixing writer interoperability bugs (CZI files libCZI could not open, PlanarConfiguration=2 TIFFs, a TIFF predictor 3 codec that did not implement predictor 3).

integration.form: module (Python package: PyPI wheels, about 40 compiled extensions); the TIFF LZW codec is also a C source-drop (3rdparty/oc_tifflzw/)
integration.dependencies: numpy and platformdirs at runtime (h5py, zarr optional). The wheels bundle libjxl, libavif, libheif, libwebp, libdeflate, libspng, libjpeg-turbo, OpenJPEG, OpenJPH 0.31.0, c-blosc2, CharLS, zstd, lz4, brotli and others. A source install uses the system libraries it finds and skips the missing ones.
integration.min_toolchain: CPython 3.10-3.13 wheels; source builds need a C/C++17 compiler, Cython, and CMake 3.16+ for the source-built libjxl (bench/build_libjxl.sh). TurboJPEG v3 API (libjpeg-turbo 3.x) is required for the jpeg codec.
integration.platforms: Wheels for macOS 15+ arm64, Linux x86_64 and aarch64 (manylinux_2_28), and Windows amd64. Intel Macs and older macOS install from the sdist.
integration.thread_safety: Codec calls release the GIL (nogil blocks), and the README benchmarks eight concurrent TIFF readers. JPEG 2000, JPEG XL and BCn spawn their own threads per call by default. No formal thread-safety statement found.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it reads and writes the same formats and bitstreams as imagecodecs/tifffile (parity tests against imagecodecs), but the API differs (oc.get_codec(name).encode/decode, oc.read, own Reader objects), so call sites must change.

gotchas: Defaults differ from imagecodecs: the PNG encoder tries only the NONE, SUB and UP filters ('fast'), where libpng tries all five for 8-bit RGB. AVIF uses a fast preset (bench/README.md: about 90x faster than imagecodecs' high-quality default), and brotli defaults to level 6, not 1. Equal-looking calls can therefore produce different bytes and speeds.

The opencodecs 0.5.0 Linux wheel bundles libjxl 0.11.2 (the wheel workflow pins LIBJXL_VERSION v0.11.2), while imagecodecs 2026.8.16 bundles 0.12.0. The README footnote says both use 0.12.0. On Linux, lossy JPEG XL decodes differ from imagecodecs' by 1 in about a third of the values, and encode sizes differ.
Do not load opencodecs and imagecodecs LERC in one process: each statically links libLerc and the second copy aborts (bench_vs_imagecodecs.py docstring and bench/README.md).

Licensing provenance: CHANGES.rst calls the project a 'fork-then-divergence' of imagecodecs. Issue #1, opened 2026-05-22 by imagecodecs' author, asks for the BSD-3 per-file copyright notices in derived files to be restored and is still open; THIRD-PARTY.md says no imagecodecs code remains beyond .pxd declarations that resemble it.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it when you work in Python and want one package that both decodes many formats and reads whole scientific containers in parallel (including over HTTP). From C or C++, use the underlying libraries directly instead: libspng plus libdeflate (or fpng/fpnge for speed over ratio) for PNG, libjpeg-turbo for JPEG, OpenJPH or Grok for JPEG 2000, bcdec for BCn. Vendor only oc_tifflzw, which applies to TIFF LZW the output-as-dictionary trick that AnimatedGIF and giflib-turbo use for GIF.
verified_claims_summary: Author's harness (bench/bench_vs_imagecodecs.py): opencodecs 0.5.0 against imagecodecs 2026.8.16 with Python 3.12, a fresh process per sample, medians over 5 shuffled rounds, identical decoded output required. Hosts were an unnamed 20-core Apple silicon Mac, a 64-core x86-64 Linux workstation pinned to one 4-core L3 group (source comments mention Zen 2) and a 4-core x86-64 Windows laptop (Kaby Lake per source comments); no CPU models or build flags are given. Reading the harness and imagecodecs' source turned up four measurement problems. (1) The harness passes the output size to opencodecs' LZW and PackBits decoders but calls imagecodecs.lzw_decode(b) and packbits_decode(b) without out=, which makes imagecodecs run a full size pre-pass (imcd_lzw_decode_size, imcd_packbits_decode_size) first. In an enricher rerun on the same PyPI wheels (opencodecs 0.5.0, imagecodecs 2026.8.16, Python 3.12, harness input, 4-vCPU Intel Xeon @ 2.80GHz container, three runs of 15 interleaved calls each), LZW decode went from 2.71-2.80x as harnessed to 2.15-2.17x with out=n. PackBits went from 1.79-1.85x to 1.02x: the README's PackBits decode win (3.32x/2.81x/1.52x) is a harness artifact, and its input expands under PackBits (16,908,288 bytes from 16,777,216). (2) The deflate and PNG rows use imagecodecs' zlib codecs, although imagecodecs ships libdeflate (deflate_encode), which matched opencodecs (519 vs 537 ms, byte-identical output). (3) The imagecodecs 2026.8.16 manylinux x86-64 wheel's libjpeg-turbo 3.2.0 has no SIMD: objdump shows 0 ymm and 0 pmaddwd instructions, against 4,133 and 565 in opencodecs' bundled copy. Rerun JPEG q90 encode was 24.8 vs 94.4 ms with identical 2,437,855-byte output, so the Linux JPEG rows (3.91x/1.80x) reflect the baseline's packaging. (4) The threaded rows compare thread counts, not per-core speed. The general compressor rows also use near-incompressible data: deflate and zstd reach about 91% of input, and lz4 and snappy output exceeds input, so their decode rows are mostly copies.
status_note: Very active single-author project (about 470 commits; PyPI 0.3.1 through 0.7.1 between 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-04; last commit 2026-10-04), BSD-3-Clause with an open attribution issue from imagecodecs' author, 3 stars; usable today as a pip-installable Python package, and its LZW C code is small enough to vendor.
